title: Tracing context hygiene and metric windowing optimizations
text:
Tracing context hygiene and metric windowing optimizations

description:
Refactor and harden tracing propagation and metrics buffering to reduce allocation spikes, avoid dropped spans during graceful shutdown, and lower cardinality pressure from transient tags. This ticket combines an OpenTelemetry SDK upgrade, a small span-shim refactor to centralize baggage/span-context logic, and a new bounded metrics window implementation to reduce tail latency caused by flush storms. Goal: measurable p75/p99 latency improvements on the serving runtime under sustained traffic, and elimination of intermittent OOM-like OTel allocation spikes observed in production.

acceptance_criteria:
1) OpenTelemetry SDK upgraded in the runtime packages with no behavior regressions in span propagation tests.
2) Tracing/context logic consolidated behind a minimal span-shim API; downstream callers must not need to touch low-level OT APIs.
3) Metrics publish path introduces bounded windowing/ring buffer with configurable max-window-size and max-emit-rate.
4) End-to-end benchmarks show at least 25% reduction in p99 CPU allocation related to tracing+metrics under representative load.
5) Graceful shutdown path drains spans/metrics within configured timeout with no dropped telemetry in integration tests.
6) Rollout plan (canary -> gradual) documented and smoke dashboards added to Console.

technical_notes:
- Upgrade plan: bump opentelemetry-java/opentelemetry-go (depending on runtime language) to a supported LTS line; prefer minor version that contains sampling and context propagation bugfixes.
- Introduce a lightweight span-shim in runtime/core/tracing that exposes: StartSpan(parentContext, meta), EndSpan(span, outcome), Inject/Extract carriers, and Baggage helpers. This avoids scattered OT imports and makes future SDK swaps easier.
- Replace ad-hoc label maps used by metrics with a shared zero-copy LabelView backed by preallocated string slice pool to cut allocations.
- Metrics window: implement a bounded ring buffer per-metric-namespace with configurable emission timer and backpressure signal to upstream callers to drop or coalesce low-priority metrics under pressure.
- Provide a fast-path for hot code paths: if context has no baggage and sampling is deterministic, avoid creating Span objects and record only counters.
- Add CI integration tests that run an instrumentation smoke harness and capture memory/alloc profiles and tracing fidelity (span parent-child correctness).
- Monitor: add temporary trace/metric flags to measure dropped telemetry and allocation deltas during rollout.

steps:
Create branch: feature/ENG-59823-tracing-hygiene
Prototype span-shim API and replace two high-traffic callers (request router, batching worker)
Upgrade OpenTelemetry dependency and run compilation + unit tests
Implement per-namespace metrics ring buffer and tune defaults (window=200ms, max_items=5000)
Add zero-copy LabelView and integrate into existing metric instruments
Add graceful shutdown drain logic and integration tests to simulate sudden process termination
Run loadbench comparing current main vs branch with tracing+metrics enabled
Create PR, gather design/eng review, and add rollout checklist in description
Canary rollout to low-traffic region, monitor allocation/telemetry metrics, then progressive rollout
